title: Wart removal
what: The wart is frozen with liquid nitrogen, which is very cold. The tissue dies and falls off after a few days.
why: If the wart bothers you, hurts, grows, or does not go away on its own.
tell_doctor: Diabetes or poor blood flow in the legs
If you do not tolerate cold well
Medicines that weaken the immune system

prepare.title: Before the procedure
prepare.text: First, a dermatologist checks the growth to make sure it is a wart.

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Do not put cream on the area. Do not try to cut the wart off yourself.

steps: The doctor looks at the wart
Sometimes the hard top layer is scraped off
Liquid nitrogen is put on the wart with a cotton swab or a device
It is held for a few seconds, and the skin turns white
Sometimes the freezing is repeated 2 to 3 times
feel: Strong cold, burning, and tingling during freezing
Afterwards, throbbing pain for a few hours
after: A blister may appear in a day or two. Do not pop it
The scab falls off on its own in 1 to 3 weeks
Often 2 to 4 treatments are needed, a few weeks apart
Keep the area clean. Cover it with a plaster if it rubs
red_flags: Redness spreading around the spot, pus, or fever
Severe pain that keeps getting worse

faq.q: How many times does a wart need freezing?
faq.a: Often 2 to 4 times, 2 to 3 weeks apart. Large warts and warts on the sole take longer.
Usually a pale spot is left, which becomes hard to notice over time.
